pages.text: Energy Pipes are the $(4)veins$(0) of your grid: they tie generators, cells and machines into one network that balances power on its own.$(br2)$(bold)Key facts:$(0)$(li)Neighbouring pipes and blocks $(4)connect automatically$(0) — anything linked shares one grid$(li)A single network holds up to $(bold)1024 pipe segments$(0), plenty for a large base$(li)Hook up a machine and power flows; several machines share it on demand$(br2)Want fine control over the flow? Every segment has a Normal / Push / Pull mode and can have one side severed — the tool is on the next page.

The $(4)Configurator$(0) is your wrench for pipes:$(li)$(bold)Right-click$(0) a pipe: cycle Normal → Push → Pull. $(bold)Normal$(0) flows both ways; $(bold)Push$(0) only feeds connected devices; $(bold)Pull$(0) only drains them$(li)$(bold)Sneak + right-click$(0) one face: $(4)sever / restore$(0) that side so power skips whatever you don't want to touch$(br2)Wired it backwards? Two clicks fix it — no need to break the pipe.

$(bold)Four tiers of transfer rate per tick$(0):$(li)Akaishi Energy Pipe: 50 thousand$(li)Advanced: 500 thousand$(li)Elite: 5 million$(li)Ultimate: 50 million$(br2)Each step is 10× the last. $(4)A Basic pipe already drives a single Generator Matrix$(0); switch to the higher tiers for a sprawling grid — $(bold)never let the pipe be the bottleneck$(0).

Run the "$(l:akaishi:generator)Energy Generator$(/l)" output through pipes into "$(l:akaishi:energy_cell)Energy Cells$(/l)" and out to every machine — that's a complete grid. Missed the fundamentals? Check "$(l:akaishi:energy_basics)Akaishi Energy Basics$(/l)".
